title: New: Enter still down on Save answers the overwrite question with Overwrite before it can be read
why: Not in the review. The Overwrite button is the first button of the second question and gets the widget id, and so the keyboard focus, that Save had; the safe answer Cancel takes the keyboard only at the end of that frame (mod.rs:358-360). A key repeat, or a second press, that arrives in the first frame of the second question presses Overwrite. In the running app a frame without events normally comes between (egui asks for one after any input), so the window is narrow, but what it loses is the other program's text.
observable: Holding Enter on Save while the file changed on disk can write over the other program's text and close the tab, with the question never seen.

title: A held arrow key is a cut point at every repeat, so its presses queue one per frame and can run on after the key is let go
why: Read at d3575c2, not run. The predicate in TypedAhead::hold (src/app/frame/mod.rs:68-73) matches any pressed Tab or arrow and ignores the event's `repeat` field, and egui delivers a key repeat as a pressed event with repeat set (egui-0.33.3 src/data/input.rs:435-442). So each frame lets in the events up to the first such press and holds every later one (:74-75), putting them ahead of the next frame's events (:65-67). When more than one repeat of a held arrow arrives per frame, the held list grows by the surplus each frame and empties at one press per frame after release. That part is certain from the code. Whether repeats outrun frames on a real machine was not measured: an ordinary repeat rate is slower than a 60 Hz frame, so it takes a slow frame or a fast repeat setting, and a slow frame is the very case the fix was written for. The three places named are as cited: the source in edit mode is a multiline TextEdit that takes the arrows itself (its focus-lock filter, egui text_edit/builder.rs:619, is honoured at the top of Focus::begin_pass, memory/mod.rs:530-540), the page scroll and the find bar bind unmodified arrows (src/app/shortcuts/mod.rs:199-207) and queue each kind of action once per frame (:224-226). In none of them does an arrow move the keyboard, so the rule costs there without fixing anything. The fix is otherwise sound by reading: nothing is dropped or duplicated, and the order of events is kept.
observable: Not observed, inferred from the code: on a slow frame or with a fast key repeat, a held arrow key keeps moving the caret in edit mode, scrolling the page, or stepping through find matches for a moment after the key is released.
size: 1 file, 2 lines, and one reader test of about 15 lines; the driver needs a way to send repeats (tap_in_turn sends `repeat: false` only, tests/reader/support/act.rs:168-182)
guards: tests/reader/unsaved.rs keys_typed_in_one_frame_answer_in_the_order_they_were_pressed and tests/reader/overwrite.rs a_move_to_overwrite_and_enter_typed_in_one_frame_overwrite send fresh presses only and stay as they are. The new test must fail today: several repeated ArrowDown presses in one frame in edit mode move the caret one line, where they should move it by all of them and leave nothing held.

code: - **Keys typed faster than the window drew were answered out of order.** `Shift+Tab` or an arrow key and then `Enter`, arriving in one frame of a slow or busy machine, pressed the button the keyboard had just left.
